title: Burst entitlement reconciliation and threshold arbitration for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Marta Liu
description:
Background: Customers on Dedicated purchase both a baseline sustained throughput commitment and a bounded burst entitlement for short windows. We lack a clear reconciliation and arbitration model for when observed throughput spikes exceed purchased burst but are still short-lived and may have been caused by cross-tenant noise, autoscaler misconfiguration, or degraded kernel performance.

Goal: Define product behavior, observability, and contract language that: (1) reconciles burst usage vs. baseline without surprising customers; (2) provides a reproducible arbitration flow for disputed overages; (3) ties autoscale policies to credit calculation and post-incident remediations; (4) produces a short, legally-reviewable contract clause and customer-facing FAQ.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Arbitration playbook documented and executable by Support/SRE within 48h.
- Grafana panels and raw metrics for burst-window reconciliation available in Console (tokens/min, scheduled batch latency, kernel-eviction events).
- Contract language reviewed by Legal and used in 2 pilot renewals (sales) without edits.
- Customer-visible overage notices are delivered within 30 minutes of threshold crossing for >95% of cases.

Scope:
- Design of reconciliation algorithm (sliding-window vs. quantile window).
- Definition of evidence package for disputes (request logs, KV-cache hit rates, autoscaler events).
- Sample contract language and notice templates.
- Observability surface (dashboards + alerting).

Out of scope:
- Fundamental rewrite of autoscaler algorithm (handled in ENG backlog).
- Legal negotiation of final enterprise contract terms for >$1M ARR customers (handled per-account).

Approach:
1) Propose a reconciliation model: 1-minute rolling peak vs. 1-hour burst budget amortization with a grace multiplier for transient infra noise.
2) Implement an evidence collector in the Console that bundles per-route token counts, per-host queue sizes, autoscale decisions, and kernel-level error logs into a digestible ZIP for arbitration.
3) Draft 3 contract clause variants (conservative / balanced / permissive) and a single-customer FAQ.
4) Run a 2-week pilot with two existing Dedicated customers who opt into the program and feed feedback into iteration.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Draft contract clause published to Confluence and approved by Legal.
- Observability prototype (dashboard + 1 alert) merged to staging and validated against historical incidents.
- Arbitration checklist and runbook documented and reviewed by Support and SRE.

Sample contract clause (for discussion):
"Burst Entitlement & Reconciliation: Customer is allocated a baseline committed throughput and a burst entitlement measured as tokens-per-minute for temporary load spikes. Redwood Inference will reconcile usage on a rolling-hour basis: transient spikes below 1.5x the committed rate are absorbed against the burst entitlement; sustained usage above this threshold will be considered committed usage and charged per the billing terms. In cases of dispute, Redwood will produce an evidence package (request logs, autoscaler events, kernel error logs) and initiate an arbitration window. If infrastructure anomalies (as defined in the arbitration rubric) materially contributed to the overage, Redwood will apply a corrective credit not to exceed the total overage charge."
